Closed-records index
Destruction Log and approvals
Staff Access List
Signed Release of Information forms
Disclosure Log
Access request forms and response dates
Breach and incident reports

policies.category: Home Serving Nine or More Individuals
policies.title: Posted Evacuation Procedures and Diagram (Homes Serving 9+)
policies.applies_to: Any [AGENCY NAME] home whose licensed capacity or number of individuals served is nine or more; all staff and individuals in that home
policies.purpose: To ensure that, in any home serving nine or more individuals, written evacuation procedures and an evacuation diagram showing the direction of egress are posted in a conspicuous place and kept accurate, so that individuals, staff and visitors can leave safely in an emergency.
policies.policy:
This policy meets 55 Pa. Code §6400.236 and Official Checklist Item 236 (RCG p.129): written emergency evacuation procedures as specified in §6400.103 (evacuation procedures), and an evacuation diagram specifying the direction for egress in the event of an emergency, shall be posted in a conspicuous place.

Applicability. This policy applies only to homes serving nine or more individuals. The licensed capacity of each home is stated on its certificate of compliance and in GR-01. [AGENCY NAME]'s home at [ADDRESS] has a licensed capacity of [LICENSED CAPACITY]. If a home serves eight or fewer individuals, the posting requirement of §6400.236 does not apply to that home. [AGENCY NAME] will still keep the written evacuation procedures required by §6400.103, in line with FS-02, and may post them voluntarily. If a home's capacity or census later reaches nine, this policy applies from the first day the ninth individual is served.

Content. Posted procedures follow §6400.103 and are tailored to the mobility, sensory and communication needs of the people living in the home (FS-02). The diagram shows the direction of egress from each part of the home, exits, and the meeting place. Both are posted in a conspicuous place where staff, individuals and visitors can see them, and are updated whenever the layout, occupancy or an individual's needs change.

definitions.definition: The written steps for leaving the home in an emergency, required by §6400.103, including routes tailored to individuals' mobility.
A floor plan of the home showing exits and the direction for egress from each area, with the person's current location marked.
A location in a common area, on each floor, that is in plain view and easy to read, such as the main hall near exits, and not behind a door or in an office.
The route and means of leaving the building to a place of safety.

procedures: At adoption, and when each home is approved, the [CEO / ADMINISTRATOR NAME] checks the home's licensed capacity on the certificate of compliance and records on the Home Applicability Sheet whether the home serves nine or more individuals. The sheet is kept in the policy file.

For any home that serves nine or more individuals, the Administrator and Program Specialist write the evacuation procedures under FS-02, following §6400.103: how the alarm is sounded, who assists which individuals, routes tailored to each person's mobility, how everyone is accounted for, and where everyone meets outside.

The Program Specialist prepares an evacuation diagram for each floor. It shows exits and the arrows for the direction of egress from each room and common area, the locations of alarms and extinguishers, the outdoor meeting place, and a 'You are here' marker.

The Administrator posts the written procedures and the diagram for each floor in a conspicuous place, in each floor's main corridor or common area, at about eye level, and in a place accessible to wheelchair users. Postings are in large, plain print and, where needed, in pictures, braille or other formats (IR-05).
Staff walk the home within the first week and confirm that postings are visible, legible and not blocked by furniture, decorations or other notices. The check is recorded on the Posting Checklist.

New staff are shown the postings and walk the routes during orientation (ST-03). New individuals are shown them within 24 hours of admission, in a way they understand, and during their first fire drill (FS-03).

The Administrator reviews the postings at least quarterly, at each fire drill, and whenever a bedroom is reassigned, an individual's mobility or needs change, walls or exits are changed, or a new individual moves in. The review is recorded.

If the layout, exits or individual needs change, the Program Specialist revises the procedures and diagram and posts them within 24 hours of the change. The old versions are removed and a dated copy kept in the home file.

If a posting is missing, damaged or illegible, any staff person who notices it informs the supervisor immediately, and a replacement is posted within 24 hours. The supervisor records the date on the Posting Checklist.

Evacuation routes are rehearsed during fire drills under FS-03. Problems seen in drills, such as blocked routes or confusion about where to go, are corrected in the posted procedures and diagram within 7 days.

If a home serves eight or fewer individuals, the Administrator notes 'Not applicable under §6400.236 - licensed capacity [LICENSED CAPACITY]' on the Applicability Sheet. The home still keeps its written evacuation procedures under §6400.103 and FS-02.
During annual self-assessment under GR-02, the Administrator checks postings in every applicable home and keeps the results in the self-assessment file.

responsibilities.duty: Determines applicability by home; ensures postings are made, updated and verified.
Writes the procedures and draws diagrams; updates them with changes in individuals' needs.
Checks that postings are visible and legible and reports defects.
Know the posted routes; report missing or blocked postings.

documentation: Home Applicability Sheet (licensed capacity and whether §6400.236 applies)
Posted written evacuation procedures and diagrams (dated copies)
Posting Checklist
Fire drill records noting route problems (FS-03)
Revision log for changes to procedures and diagrams

policies.category: Home Serving Nine or More Individuals
policies.title: Written Daily Menus (Homes Serving 9+)
policies.applies_to: Any [AGENCY NAME] community home licensed to serve nine or more individuals. Homes with a licensed capacity of eight or fewer follow NU-01 and are not subject to the written daily menu requirement of this policy.
policies.purpose: To make sure every individual living in a home serving nine or more can see in advance what meals will be served, that the written menu and any changes are actually followed, and that menus are kept for review by the Department.
policies.policy: This policy meets 55 Pa. Code §6400.243 (a) through (e) (ODP 6400 Regulatory Compliance Guide, p. 130), official item 243a-e, which applies only to homes serving nine or more individuals. (a) Written daily menu: [AGENCY NAME] will prepare a written daily menu for each day, in a form each individual can access and understand (large print, pictures or another format, see IR-05). (b) Advance access: each menu will be accessible to individuals at least one day before the menu date. (c) Changes: any change to a menu will be written and made accessible to individuals before the meal it affects. (d) Menus followed: the written menu and any written changes will be followed. A substitution is made only through a documented change. (e) Retention: each written menu, with its changes, will be kept for at least 3 months. Menus will also meet the nutrition, modified-diet and individual preference requirements in NU-01. This policy supplements NU-01 and does not replace it.

definitions.definition: A written list of the meals and snacks planned for a given calendar day, prepared before that day and made available to individuals.
Posted or provided in a place and format (including pictures, large print, audio or other formats) that each individual can reach and understand without having to ask for permission.
Any substitution, addition or omission of a planned meal, snack or major menu item after the menu has been made accessible.
A community home whose certificate of compliance states a licensed capacity of nine or more individuals.

procedures: 1. The Administrator identifies in writing each [AGENCY NAME] home with a licensed capacity of nine or more, using the certificate of compliance (GR-01), and assigns a Menu Coordinator for each such home.
2. The Menu Coordinator prepares the written daily menu for every day of the week, including weekends and holidays, using the approved menu cycle and the nutrition requirements in NU-01.

3. Before finalizing menus, the Menu Coordinator reviews each individual's modified diet orders, food allergies, choking-risk plan, cultural or religious preferences and stated food choices (NU-01, IH-03, IR-03) and adjusts menu items accordingly.
4. The Menu Coordinator prepares each day's menu no later than 1 day before the menu date, and in all cases makes it accessible to individuals at least 1 day before the menu date.

5. The menu is posted in a common area at a height and location individuals can reach, and also provided in each individual's preferred format (large print, pictures, audio, or reviewed verbally with staff) per IR-05. The posting location is recorded in the home's procedures file.
6. Each menu shows the date, the meals and snacks planned, and the name or initials of the person who prepared it and the date and time it was made accessible.

7. If a menu must change (for example, an item is unavailable, an individual requests a different meal, or a diet order changes), the shift lead writes the change on the posted menu or on a menu change sheet, with date, time, reason and initials.
8. The shift lead makes the change accessible to individuals in advance of the affected meal, by updating the posted menu and telling each individual, using the individual's communication method.
9. Staff serving meals follow the written menu and any written changes. Staff do not substitute meals without recording a change under Step 7.
10. Substitutions are of comparable nutritional value and must still honor each individual's modified diet, allergies and choking-risk plan.
11. If an individual wants something different from the posted menu, staff support the individual's choice (IR-03) and record it as a menu change, so long as it meets that individual's diet order.
12. The Menu Coordinator files each completed daily menu, with its change sheets, in the home's menu binder or secure electronic file, organized by date.
13. Menus and changes are retained for at least 3 months from the menu date. The Menu Coordinator removes menus only after that period and no menu is discarded sooner.
14. Weekly, the Menu Coordinator compares a sample of posted menus, change records and meals actually served, and records any meal served without a documented change.
15. The Program Specialist reviews the menu records monthly, as part of the quality review (GOV-02), and retrains staff when meals were not served as written or changes were not documented.

16. The Administrator confirms during the annual self-assessment (GR-02) that menus were prepared, accessible in advance, followed, changed only by documented change, and retained for at least 3 months.

responsibilities.duty: Identifies homes serving nine or more, assigns a Menu Coordinator, ensures this policy is carried out and menus are available for Department review.
Prepares daily menus, makes them accessible at least 1 day ahead, files them and keeps them at least 3 months.
Make menu changes accessible before the meal, follow the written menu and changes, and document every change.
Reviews menu records monthly, confirms individual preferences and diet orders are reflected, and retrains staff as needed.
Advises on modified diets and nutrition so that menus meet each individual's health needs (NU-01, IH-03).

documentation: Written daily menus for each day, with preparer name/initials and date and time made accessible
Menu change sheets or annotated menus showing date, time, reason, and staff initials
Record of the posting location and alternate formats used
Weekly menu-versus-meals-served check notes
Monthly Program Specialist review notes
Retention log showing menus kept at least 3 months

policies.title: Emergency Placement
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] community homes and all staff involved in an emergency placement. An emergency placement is an admission made on short notice because an individual urgently needs a home.
policies.purpose: To allow [AGENCY NAME] to respond safely to an urgent request for a place to live without exceeding licensed capacity, and to complete the health, financial and planning steps that must follow an emergency placement on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] may accept an emergency placement only if a vacancy exists within the licensed capacity stated on the home's certificate of compliance (55 Pa. Code §6400.13). Licensed capacity is never exceeded, including for emergencies. No individual is placed in a home where the home cannot meet that person's needs safely with current staffing (ST-02). The supports coordinator is notified at once. Emergency information and a physical examination record are obtained as soon as possible, within the time limits set by Chapter 6400. The room and board agreement, Form DP 1077, is completed within 15 days of the emergency placement (ODP Bulletin 00-25-01). Individual rights, funds protection and person-centered planning begin on the day of arrival.

definitions.definition: An unplanned admission, arranged on short notice, because the individual has an urgent need for residential services (for example, loss of caregiver or housing).
The maximum number of individuals the certificate of compliance permits at the home's location. It may not be exceeded.
The Department's mandatory room and board agreement form, required before admission, annually, and within 15 days of an emergency placement.
The person from the county Administrative Entity or Supports Coordination Organization responsible for the individual's service plan.

procedures: 1. When a request for emergency placement is received, the staff member taking the call refers it immediately to the Administrator or designee on call ([PHONE]).

2. The Administrator confirms the current census against licensed capacity on the certificate of compliance (GR-01). If accepting the person would put the home above its licensed capacity, the request is declined and the supports coordinator is told so immediately.
3. The Administrator confirms bedroom and bathroom space meet the requirements in PS-01 for the additional individual, and that sleeping arrangements respect privacy and compatibility (IR-03).

4. The Administrator and Program Specialist review available information about the person (needs, medical issues, behavior supports, supervision level) and decide whether staff can safely meet those needs with current staffing and training (ST-02, ST-04). The decision and reasons are documented.
5. If accepted, the Administrator notifies the supports coordinator at once, by phone, and confirms in writing the same day, including the expected arrival date and time.

6. Before or at arrival, staff obtain all available emergency information: name, emergency contacts, guardian or representative, physician, insurance, allergies, medications, diagnoses and communication needs (REC-01).

7. Staff obtain a physical examination record as soon as possible. If none is available at arrival, the Nurse arranges an examination or obtains the most recent record, within the time limits in Chapter 6400, and the Administrator tracks the due date (IH-01).
8. On the day of arrival, staff inform the individual and representative of the individual's rights in a way they understand and record that this was done (IR-01).
9. Staff inventory and record the individual's personal property and money on arrival, and begin the funds ledger (GR-08).
10. The Nurse reviews medications brought with the person and obtains current medication orders before any dose is given (MD-01, MD-03).
11. The Program Specialist begins interim support instructions the day of arrival and arranges the planning meeting with the supports coordinator and the individual's team (PG-02).

12. The Administrator completes Form DP 1077 with the individual and representative within 15 days of the placement date, applying the room and board limits in GOV-04, and gives them a copy. The due date is logged on the day of placement.

13. The Administrator makes sure that no room and board is charged for any period that is respite rather than residential placement (see RC-01), and that the form reflects the individual's actual status.
14. The Administrator reports any incident during the placement under GR-04 and records the emergency placement in the home's admission log.

15. Within 30 days of arrival, the Program Specialist and supports coordinator confirm whether the placement will continue or the individual will transition elsewhere, and PG-04 applies if services end.

responsibilities.duty: Approves or declines each emergency placement, confirms capacity, notifies the supports coordinator, and completes Form DP 1077 within 15 days.
Assesses needs against staffing, starts interim supports and arranges planning.
Obtains the physical exam record and medication orders and reviews health needs.
Welcome the individual, gather emergency information, inform the individual of rights, inventory belongings and follow interim supports.
Receives periodic reports on emergency placements and any capacity concerns (GOV-02).

documentation: Emergency placement request log with date, time, and decision
Census and licensed-capacity check
Staffing and needs assessment note
Record of supports coordinator notification (date, time, person)
Emergency information sheet and physical examination record
Record of rights information given to the individual
Property and funds inventory
Form DP 1077, signed and dated, with the 15-day due-date log

policies.title: Respite Care
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] community homes and all staff, if the governing body approves offering respite care. Respite may not be offered in any home until Step 1 below is complete.
policies.purpose: To make sure any short-term respite stay is safe, planned, and consistent with licensed capacity, staffing ratios, individual rights and the rule that room and board is not charged during respite.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not offer respite until the Administrator has reviewed the respite provisions of Chapter 6400 and recorded that review, and the governing body has approved the service (GOV-01). A person staying for respite counts toward the home's licensed capacity stated on the certificate of compliance (55 Pa. Code §6400.13) and toward staffing ratios (ST-02); a respite stay may never cause the home to exceed licensed capacity or required staffing. [AGENCY NAME] does not charge room and board during respite (ODP Bulletin 00-25-01). A respite guest has the same rights, health and safety protections, medication safeguards and incident reporting protections as any other individual in the home.

definitions.definition: Short-term, temporary care in the home that gives the individual's usual caregiver a break. It is not a permanent residential admission.
An individual who stays in the home temporarily under a respite plan.
The maximum number of individuals the certificate of compliance permits at the home. Respite guests are counted.

procedures: 1. Before any respite is offered, the Administrator reviews the respite provisions of Chapter 6400 and the funding rules for respite, records the review and obtains written approval from the governing body (GOV-01). Respite is not offered until this is done.

2. When a respite request is received, the Administrator checks the dates against the current census and licensed capacity (GR-01). Respite is declined if the stay would put the home over capacity on any night.
3. The Administrator confirms that staff scheduled for the dates meet the ratios and supervision needs for all individuals including the guest (ST-02).

4. The Program Specialist reviews the guest's needs, behavior supports, communication, and compatibility with current residents (IR-03) and decides in writing whether the home can safely serve the guest.

5. Before the stay, the Administrator or Program Specialist obtains from the guest or representative: emergency contacts, physician, insurance, allergies, diagnoses, current medication orders, supervision needs, support plan and any health care instructions (REC-01).
6. The Nurse reviews medications and orders before arrival. Medications are given only by certified staff under MD-01, and stored per MD-02.
7. On arrival, staff tell the guest, in a way they understand, about the home rules and the individual's rights, and record that they did so (IR-01).
8. Staff inventory the guest's belongings and any money held, and return them at departure (GR-08).

9. The Administrator makes sure no room and board is charged for respite days, and billing for respite follows GOV-03 and the applicable ODP service rules. Fees are not collected from the guest for room and board.
10. Staff record daily notes for the guest and follow the guest's support plan (PG-02).
11. Any incident involving the guest is reported under GR-04 and investigated under GR-05, with notification to the guest's representative and supports coordinator.
12. In an emergency, staff follow IH-02 and FS-02 for the guest exactly as for any other individual, and contact the representative immediately.
13. At the end of the stay, staff return medications, belongings and written notes to the guest or representative and record the departure time.

14. If a respite stay is expected to become permanent, the Administrator stops the respite arrangement and uses PG-01, including Form DP 1077 and an admission within licensed capacity. If it was an urgent placement, EP-01 applies.
15. The Administrator reviews respite stays quarterly with the governing body (GOV-02) and records any capacity, staffing or incident concerns.

responsibilities.duty: Decides whether to offer respite and approves it only after the Chapter 6400 review is recorded.
Checks capacity and staffing, accepts or declines requests, ensures no room and board is charged and oversees billing.
Assesses compatibility and needs and ensures the guest's support plan is followed.
Reviews health information and medication orders.
Provide care, document daily, protect the guest's rights and property, and report incidents.

documentation: Governing body approval and record of Chapter 6400 respite review
Respite request and decision log
Census and capacity check per stay
Staffing schedule for stay dates
Guest emergency information, medication orders and support plan
Rights notice record
Property inventory and return receipt
Daily notes and incident reports
Billing record confirming no room and board charge

policies.title: Governing Body, Provider Enrollment, Policy Review and Regulatory Waivers
policies.applies_to: The governing body, the Administrator, and all management staff of [AGENCY NAME].
policies.purpose: To establish who is legally responsible for [AGENCY NAME], to ensure licensure and ODP enrollment are properly maintained, to keep policies current, and to control any request for relief from a regulation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by its governing body, which holds final legal responsibility for the agency, its homes and its compliance. The legal entity is named exactly as on the application for certificate of compliance, on all licenses, ODP enrollment records, contracts, and policies. A certificate of compliance is required before any home operates (55 Pa. Code §6400.11). The application is made on the Department-prescribed form (HS-633), one application per home, and no home operates until the Department notifies [AGENCY NAME] that a certificate will issue (55 Pa. Code §20.21). ODP provider enrollment is separate from licensure; new residential providers enroll through ODP's competitive Request for Application (RFA) process, in effect since 1/1/2025. Policies are reviewed at least annually and a version history is kept. Regulatory waiver requests are sent to ra-odplicensing@pa.gov only after 30 days' written notice to affected individuals. The governing body also oversees ODP residential performance standards effective 1/1/2026, which affect Select and Clinically Enhanced status.

definitions.definition: The board of directors, owner(s) or other group with final legal authority over [AGENCY NAME].
The Department's license for a community home, stating the home's location and maximum capacity.
Approval by the Office of Developmental Programs to deliver and bill for waiver services. It is separate from licensure.
Written approval by the Department allowing [AGENCY NAME] to deviate from a specific regulatory requirement.
The exact name of the corporation, LLC or other entity filed with the Commonwealth and shown on the application.

procedures: 1. The governing body meets at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., quarterly], keeps minutes, and records its decisions on policy, budget, licensure, enrollment, waivers and quality oversight.
2. The governing body appoints the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]) and confirms in writing the Administrator's authority and qualifications (ST-01).

3. Before opening each home, the Administrator confirms the legal entity name matches exactly across the application, local business filings, the certificate of occupancy, insurance and ODP enrollment records, and corrects any differences before submission.
4. The Administrator submits one application on the Department-prescribed form for each home (55 Pa. Code §20.21), with all required attachments, and keeps a copy and proof of submission.

5. No individual is admitted and no services are provided in a home until the Department has notified [AGENCY NAME] that a certificate of compliance will issue (GR-01). The Administrator records the date of that notice.

6. The Administrator tracks ODP provider enrollment separately: confirms the competitive RFA status, qualification requirements, and the effective date of enrollment, and does not bill for services before enrollment is effective (GOV-03).
7. The Administrator tracks the ODP residential performance standards effective 1/1/2026 and reports results to the governing body at least quarterly (GOV-02).
8. The Administrator reviews every policy and procedure at least annually. Reviews are recorded with the reviewer name, date and any changes made.
9. Each policy carries a version number, effective date and revision history. Superseded versions are kept in an archive and not circulated.
10. When regulations, ODP bulletins or agency practice change, the Administrator updates affected policies promptly rather than waiting for the annual review, and trains staff on changes (ST-04).
11. The governing body approves new and revised policies by recorded vote, and the approval date is noted on each policy.
12. Before requesting any regulatory waiver, the Administrator documents the regulation, the reason, the alternative that protects individuals' health, safety and rights, and the proposed duration.

13. The Administrator gives each affected individual and representative written notice of the waiver request, in a format they understand, at least 30 days before submission, and records how comments were considered (IR-01, IR-05).

14. After the 30-day notice period, the Administrator sends the waiver request to ra-odplicensing@pa.gov and keeps the submission, the notice and any response. The requested deviation does not begin until the Department approves it in writing.
15. The Administrator keeps approved waivers on file, calendars expiration dates, and checks conditions during the annual self-assessment (GR-02).

16. The Administrator reports to the governing body any citation, plan of correction, enforcement action or change of ownership or management as soon as it occurs, and the governing body decides on corrective action.
17. The governing body reviews this policy annually, along with agency licensure status, enrollment status, insurance and quality results.

policies.title: Quality Improvement, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, Program Specialist, Nurse, quality designee and the governing body of [AGENCY NAME], for all homes and all individuals served.
policies.purpose: To use incident data, self-assessment results, performance measures and death reviews to improve the safety and quality of life of individuals, and to hold the governing body accountable for the results.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates a quality improvement program overseen by the governing body. Incident trends are analyzed and reviewed at least every 3 months, as required by 55 Pa. Code §6400.20 (see GR-06). Each home is self-assessed under 55 Pa. Code §6400.15 (see GR-02), and results feed this program. ODP residential performance measures are tracked and reported. Every death of an individual is reviewed, and the outcome is reported to the governing body (IH-04). The program identifies problems, assigns corrective actions with owners and due dates, and checks whether the actions worked.

definitions.definition: A regular process of collecting data, finding problems or risks, taking corrective action and measuring results.
A pattern in incidents by type, individual, location, time, staff or cause that suggests a risk needing action.
A structured review of the circumstances, care and any preventable factors surrounding an individual's death.
A defined ODP residential performance standard or indicator the agency tracks and reports.

procedures: 1. The governing body designates the Administrator as quality improvement lead and names a quality designee in writing: [QUALITY DESIGNEE NAME].

2. The quality designee compiles incident data from all homes at least every 3 months: counts by type, individual, home, shift, time of day, location, injury, and cause, using the incident reports (GR-04, GR-05).

3. The Administrator, Program Specialist and Nurse meet at least every 3 months to review the data and the incident analysis in GR-06, looking for trends and for prevention actions for individuals and homes.
4. For each trend or risk, the team writes a corrective or preventive action with a responsible person and a due date, and records it in the quality action log.
5. The quality designee follows each action to completion, and at the next quarterly review checks whether incidents of that type have decreased. Actions that did not work are revised.
6. The Administrator reviews results of each home's self-assessment (GR-02, 55 Pa. Code §6400.15) and the Department's inspection findings, and adds any deficiencies to the quality action log.
7. The quality designee tracks ODP residential performance measures as published by ODP and updates the results at least quarterly, comparing them to the agency's targets.

8. The Administrator reviews grievances and complaints (GR-09), rights restrictions (RP-01), restraint use (RP-02), medication errors (MD-03), and missing-person events (PG-05) as part of each quarterly review.

9. Within [NUMBER, e.g., 14] days of each individual death, the Administrator convenes a mortality review including the Nurse and Program Specialist (and a physician consultant, if available). It reviews the circumstances, health history, care provided, response to the emergency, incident reports, and any prevention opportunity (IH-04).

10. The Administrator writes up the mortality review, with findings and recommended actions, and reports it to the governing body at its next meeting, or sooner if there is a serious concern. Confidentiality is protected (IR-04).

11. The Administrator presents a written quality report to the governing body at least every 3 months, covering incident trends, corrective actions and results, self-assessment findings, performance measures, grievances and deaths.
12. The governing body reviews the report, records its questions and decisions in the minutes, and directs further action where results are not acceptable.
13. Staff are told about changes made because of quality findings, and training is updated where needed (ST-04).
14. Individuals and families are invited to give input on quality, through surveys, meetings or the grievance process, and results are used in the review (GR-09, IR-01).
15. The Administrator reviews this policy annually (GOV-01).

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, billing staff, Program Specialist, Nurse and all direct support staff of [AGENCY NAME] who deliver, document or bill ODP waiver Residential Habilitation.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services actually delivered to enrolled individuals, in accordance with the person-centered plan and ODP rules, and that billing is accurate, documented and auditable.
policies.policy: ODP is the effective single payer for Residential Habilitation, and its fee schedule rates are the maximum rates payable. [AGENCY NAME] bills only the rate for the individual's approved service, needs group and authorization, and never bills more than the ODP maximum. Billed days are reconciled to attendance and daily service documentation every month. [AGENCY NAME] will confirm with ODP whether electronic visit verification (EVV, 42 USC 1396b(l)) applies to community-home Residential Habilitation, and will comply if it does. [AGENCY NAME] will also confirm with ODP the billing procedure codes (for example W9000) and the delivery system used for claims, before submitting any claim. Staff never falsify, backfill without notation, or alter service records.

definitions.definition: The maximum amount ODP pays per unit for a waiver service, set by ODP.
Comparing billed units to attendance logs, daily notes and the authorization to confirm each billed day is supported.
Electronic visit verification, a federal requirement (42 USC 1396b(l)) to electronically verify certain home-based services, applicable only if ODP states it applies to this service.
ODP's approval of a specific service, amount and period for an individual in the person-centered plan.

procedures: 1. The governing body designates the Administrator as Medicaid compliance lead and names a billing designee in writing: [BILLING DESIGNEE NAME].

2. Before billing begins, the Administrator confirms with ODP in writing the correct procedure codes (for example W9000), rate modifiers, needs group and the claims delivery system, and files the answer.

3. The Administrator also asks ODP in writing whether EVV applies to community-home Residential Habilitation. If yes, the Administrator sets up EVV before billing and trains staff. If no, the written answer is filed and revisited when ODP issues new guidance.

4. For each individual, the billing designee checks that the person is enrolled, that the service is authorized in the person-centered plan, and that the authorization dates and needs group match before billing (PG-02).
5. Direct support staff complete daily service documentation for each individual each day, including date, service delivered and staff signature or initials (PG-02).

6. The billing designee bills only units supported by documentation and never bills days when the individual was absent in a way that makes the day non-billable under ODP rules, or during periods ODP does not pay for. Respite and emergency placement billing follow the applicable ODP rules (RC-01, EP-01).

7. Rates used are no higher than the current ODP fee schedule rate for the individual's needs group. The billing designee checks the current rate table each time ODP publishes an update and records the effective date.

8. Each month, before or immediately after claims are submitted, the billing designee reconciles billed days to the attendance log, the census, and the daily service notes for each individual, and records discrepancies.
9. The Administrator reviews the monthly reconciliation, signs it, and approves corrections. Any billed day that is not supported is corrected, voided or refunded promptly.
10. Room and board is handled separately from waiver billing under GOV-04 and is not billed to ODP as a waiver service.
11. The Administrator keeps copies of claims, remittances and rejections, and reviews unpaid or denied claims each month.
12. If an overpayment or billing error is found, the Administrator investigates, corrects it, repays the amount promptly, documents the cause and takes steps to prevent recurrence.

13. Any staff member who is asked to alter documentation or bill for services not delivered must refuse and report it to the Administrator or governing body, without retaliation. Suspected fraud is reported to the governing body and, where required, to the appropriate authority.
14. Staff are trained on documentation and billing rules at orientation and annually (ST-03, ST-04).
15. Records supporting claims are kept as required in REC-02 and are available to ODP, auditors and other authorized reviewers.
16. The Administrator reports billing accuracy, reconciliation results and any corrections to the governing body at least every 3 months (GOV-02), and reviews this policy annually (GOV-01).

policies.title: Room and Board Agreements and Personal Needs Allowance
policies.applies_to: All individuals receiving licensed Residential Habilitation in a [AGENCY NAME] community home under 55 Pa. Code Chapter 6400. Applies to the Administrator, business/billing staff, Program Specialist, home managers and any staff who handle individual funds or talk with individuals, families or support coordinators about charges.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] charges each individual for room and board only as allowed by the Department of Human Services Office of Developmental Programs (ODP). Every charge must be set out in a signed written agreement. Each individual must keep the personal needs allowance and have enough personal funds for his or her own use.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will have a Room and Board Agreement on Form DP 1077 in place for every individual receiving Residential Habilitation, as required by ODP (C57, C58). The agreement will be completed before admission, renewed every year, and completed within 15 days of an emergency placement (C58). The room and board charge will never exceed the regulatory cap (C56). The cap is the lowest of the following: 72% of the sum of the SSI maximum and the Pennsylvania State Supplement; 72% of the individual's total income when that income is below the SSI maximum; 40% of that amount for room only; 32% for board only; or the actual documented cost. The charge is $0 if the individual's income is below the personal needs allowance. The individual keeps the personal needs allowance (C56). [AGENCY NAME] will not charge room and board for any period of respite (C58). Board will not be charged starting on the 8th consecutive day of leave or hospitalization. Room will not be charged after more than 30 consecutive days of hospitalization (C58). [AGENCY NAME] will give at least 30 days' written notice before any increase that would reduce an individual's personal funds (C58). The agency will not use the Room and Board Agreement to restrict an individual's access to his or her own money, which is governed by GR-08 and IR-02. Dollar amounts in this policy are not fixed here. The 2026 federal SSI benefit rate is $994 per month, and the Administrator will confirm the current State Supplement, personal needs allowance and cap formula with ODP before each agreement is prepared or renewed (C56).

definitions.definition: The written agreement on Form DP 1077 (completed with ODP Attachment 4 where ODP requires it) that states what the individual is charged for room and board and what the individual keeps for personal use.
The portion of the individual's monthly income that the individual keeps for personal use and that the agency may not take as a room and board charge.
The amount an individual pays the provider for housing (room) and food (board), within the regulatory cap.

The maximum charge allowed: 72% of SSI maximum plus State Supplement (or 72% of total income if income is below the SSI maximum), 40% for room only, 32% for board only, or actual documented cost, whichever applies and is lowest.
Admission of an individual to a home on short notice because of an urgent need, handled under EP-01.
Short-term, temporary care provided under RC-01. No room and board is charged during respite.

procedures: Before each admission, the Administrator (or designee) asks the individual, family or legal representative and the support coordinator for current income information (for example SSI award letter, State Supplement, Social Security or other income). The information is filed in the individual's record.

The Administrator confirms with ODP the current State Supplement amount, personal needs allowance and cap formula. The Administrator records the date and source of the confirmation. The 2026 SSI federal rate of $994 per month is only one input to the calculation.

The business staff member calculates the maximum allowable charge using the cap in this policy: 72% of SSI plus State Supplement (or of total income where income is below the SSI maximum), 40% for room only, 32% for board only, or actual documented cost. They apply the lowest figure that applies. The charge is $0 if income is below the personal needs allowance.
The Administrator reviews and signs off on the calculation and the supporting documentation of actual cost before any figure is placed on a form.

The Program Specialist or Administrator completes Form DP 1077 (with ODP Attachment 4 where required) before the individual's admission date. The agreement is not completed after admission for planned admissions.

The Program Specialist reviews the agreement with the individual and his or her family or legal representative in plain language, using the individual's preferred communication method (see IR-05). The review covers the amount charged, what it covers, the personal needs allowance the individual keeps, the leave, hospital and respite rules, and how to file a grievance (GR-09).

The individual (or legal representative) and the agency Administrator sign and date the agreement. The individual or representative receives a copy. The support coordinator receives a copy as ODP requires. The original is filed in the individual's record (REC-01).

For an emergency placement (EP-01), the Administrator completes and signs Form DP 1077 within 15 days of the placement date. The business staff member diarizes the 15th day at the time of placement and the Administrator checks that it is done.

Business staff keep a tracking log of every individual's agreement date and renewal due date. The Administrator reviews the log monthly and each agreement is renewed annually, no later than its anniversary date.

At each annual renewal, business staff recalculate the maximum charge using current income information and current ODP figures, and the Administrator reviews it. If an individual's income has changed, the charge is adjusted within the cap.

When any charge increase would reduce the individual's personal funds, the Administrator gives written notice to the individual and legal representative at least 30 days before the increase takes effect. The notice states the old and new amount, the effective date and how to ask questions or file a grievance. The support coordinator is copied, and a copy is filed in the record.
The agency does not charge room and board for any day of respite service (RC-01). Business staff exclude respite days from billing and from any monthly statement to the respite individual.

When an individual is on leave or hospitalized, the home manager notifies business staff of the first day. Business staff stop board charges starting on the 8th consecutive day of leave or hospitalization and stop room charges if the hospitalization lasts more than 30 consecutive days. They resume charges on return in line with the agreement and ODP guidance.

Business staff make sure the individual's personal needs allowance is available to the individual each month and is deposited, tracked and spent under GR-08. The agency does not deduct fees, fines, damages, program costs or other charges from the allowance.

Business staff issue a monthly written statement to the individual (and representative) showing income received, room and board charged and amount remaining for personal use. The Administrator reviews statements quarterly for accuracy.

If an individual or representative disagrees with a charge, staff accept the concern as a grievance under GR-09. The Administrator reviews the calculation within 5 business days, corrects any overcharge in writing and refunds any overcharge to the individual promptly. The refund is documented.

If an individual is discharged or transitions (PG-04), business staff prorate the charge to the last day of service, return any remaining personal funds and the final accounting to the individual or representative, and close out the agreement in the record.

The Administrator reports the results of agreement completion, renewals, notices and refunds to the governing body in the annual review of GOV-01 and uses them in the compliance review under GOV-03. Late or missing agreements are corrected immediately and the cause is recorded.

documents.title: 55 Pa. Code Chapter 6400 Regulatory Compliance Guide (RCG) – Community Homes for Individuals with an Intellectual Disability or Autism
documents.form_number: None (companion to 55 Pa. Code Ch. 6400; Appendix A is the Self-Assessment Licensing Inspection Instrument)
documents.issuer: PA DHS Office of Developmental Programs (ODP), Regulatory Administration / Licensing
documents.version: March 15, 2023 Edition. This is the current edition on the MyODP Licensing page, and it replaces the Feb. 3, 2020 edition listed in the regulations input.
documents.how_used: No single policy checklist could be read, so this is the fallback the task allows. The RCG reproduces each 6400 regulation verbatim, with ODP's discussion and the inspection procedures licensing staff use. I pulled every provision that requires a written policy, procedure or plan (Part A). I also pulled provisions that the RCG says licensing staff check through 'applicable policies' (Part B). Item numbering follows the RCG, e.g. '22a', '110h', '243a-e'.

documents.title: NEW 6400 Policy Review List – Community Homes for Individuals with Intellectual Disabilities
documents.issuer: PA DHS ODP (posted on MyODP Licensing and Regulations page, dated 29 Mar 2022)
documents.how_used: This looks like the official new-applicant policy review document. The file came back as compressed binary, so I could not read its items and did not use it to build the list. The applicant should download it and reconcile it against the items below. Where it uses its own numbering or order, that should override this list. The MyODP page also lists a 'Checklist for the Initial Application (Appendix A)' and a 'New Applicant Licensing Flow Chart'.

required_items.text: There shall be a written policy that establishes procedures for the protection and adequate accounting of individual funds and property and for counseling the individual concerning the use of funds and property.
required_items.cite: RCG p.33; 55 Pa. Code §6400.22(a). The RCG says the policy must show how it protects funds, protects personal property, and specifies counseling based on each individual's needs, and strongly recommends referencing 22b-22g.

required_items.text: The home's policy may not prohibit the individual's right to manage the individual's own finances.
The home shall have written grievance procedures for individuals, individual's families, advocates, and staff persons that assure investigation and resolution of complaints.
required_items.cite: RCG p.35; §6400.23. Waiver providers also have Ch. 6100.51(a)-(h) complaint requirements, which I did not read.

required_items.text: The provider shall assist the affected individuals to negotiate choices in accordance with the provider's procedures for the individuals to resolve differences and make choices.
required_items.cite: RCG p.51; §6400.33(b). The RCG says the procedures must describe how differences are resolved, how choice is promoted and protected without significant health and safety risk, and must not violate any rights.

required_items.text: There shall be written emergency evacuation procedures that include individual and staff responsibilities, means of transportation and an emergency shelter location.
There shall be a written procedure for fire safety monitoring in the event the smoke detector or fire alarm is inoperative.
If an individual or staff person smokes at the home, there shall be written smoking safety procedures.
required_items.cite: RCG p.88; §6400.114(a). 114b requires the procedures to be followed.

required_items.text: The home shall have a written emergency medical plan listing the following: 1. The hospital or source of health care that will be used in an emergency. 2. The method of transportation to be used. An emergency staffing plan.
required_items.cite: RCG p.93; §6400.145. The RCG says the plan is person-specific.

required_items.text: The home shall develop and implement a written policy that defines the prohibition or use of specific types of restrictive procedures, describes the circumstances in which restrictive procedures may be used, the staff persons who may authorize the use of restrictive procedures, and a mechanism to monitor and control the use of restrictive procedures.
required_items.cite: RCG p.124; §6400.192. The RCG says the policy must be agency-wide and individual-specific and address all elements of the Restrictive Procedures section unless the agency forbids all restrictive procedures.

required_items.text: Written emergency evacuation procedures as specified in §6400.103 (relating to evacuation procedures) and an evacuation diagram specifying direction for egress in the event of an emergency, shall be posted in a conspicuous place.
required_items.cite: RCG p.129; §6400.236. Applies only to homes serving nine or more individuals.

required_items.text: (a) A written daily menu shall be prepared and accessible to an individual. (b) The menu shall be accessible to an individual at least 1 day prior to the menu date. (c) A change to a menu shall be accessible to an individual in advance of the meal. (d) A written menu and changes to the menu shall be followed. (e) A written menu shall be retained for at least 3 months.
required_items.cite: RCG p.130; §6400.243. Applies only to homes serving nine or more individuals.

required_items.text: Abuse of an individual is prohibited. Abuse is an act or omission of an act that willfully deprives an individual of rights or human dignity or which may cause or causes actual physical injury or emotional harm to an individual, such as striking or kicking an individual; neglect; rape; sexual molestation, sexual exploitation, or sexual harassment of an individual; sexual contact between a staff person and an individual; restraining an individual without following the requirements in this chapter; financial exploitation of an individual; humiliating an individual; or withholding regularly scheduled meals.
required_items.cite: RCG p.23; §6400.16. PART B: the regulation does not say 'written policy'. I included it because abuse prohibition, discipline and reporting are normal policy content.

required_items.text: The home shall immediately report abuse or suspected abuse of an individual 17 years of age or younger to ChildLine 1(800) 932-0313.

The home shall report the following incidents, alleged incidents and suspected incidents through the Department's information management system or on a form specified by the Department within 24 hours of discovery by a staff person: 1. Death. 2. A physical act by an individual in attempt to complete suicide. 3. Inpatient admission to a hospital. 4. Abuse, including individual to individual abuse. 5. Neglect. 6. Exploitation. 7. An individual who is missing for more than 24 hours or who could be in jeopardy if missing at all. 8. Law enforcement activity that occurs during the provision of a service or for which an individual is the subject of a law enforcement investigation that may lead to criminal charges against the individual. 9. Injury requiring treatment beyond first aid. 10. Fire requiring the services of the fire department not including false alarms. 11. Emergency closure. 12. Theft or misuse of individual funds. 13. A violation of individual rights.
required_items.cite: RCG p.24; §6400.18(a). PART B: the RCG says licensing staff verify through 'applicable policies' and calls incident policies and procedures an essential component.

required_items.text: The home shall report the following incidents, alleged incidents and suspected incidents through the Department's information management system or on a form specified by the Department within 72 hours of discovery by a staff person: 1. Use of restraint. A medication error as specified in §6400.167 (relating to medication errors), if the medication was ordered by a health care practitioner.
The individual and persons designated by the individual shall be notified within 24 hours of discovery of an incident relating to the individual.
required_items.cite: RCG p.25; §6400.18(c). 18d requires keeping documentation of the notification. PART B.

required_items.text: The incident report, or a summary of the incident, the finding, and the actions taken, redacted to exclude information about another individual and the reporter, unless the reporter is the individual who receives the report, shall be available to the individual and persons designated by the individual upon request.
The home shall take immediate action to protect the health, safety, and well-being of the individual following the initial knowledge or notice of an incident, alleged incident, or suspected incident.
The home shall initiate an investigation of an incident, alleged incident, or suspected incident within 24 hours of discovery by a staff person.
required_items.cite: RCG p.27; §6400.18(g). PART B. The RCG says providers must have access to a Certified Investigator at all times.

required_items.text: A Department-certified incident investigator shall conduct the investigation of the following incidents: 1. Death that occurs during the provision of service. 2. Inpatient admission to a hospital as a result of an accidental or unexplained injury or an injury caused by a staff person, another individual or during the use of a restraint. 3. Abuse. 4. Neglect. 5. Exploitation. 6. Injury requiring treatment beyond first aid as a result of an accidental or unexplained injury or an injury caused by a staff person, another individual or during the use of a restraint. 7. Theft or misuse of individual funds. 8. A violation of individual rights.

The home shall finalize the incident report through the Department's information management system or on a form specified by the Department within 30 days of discovery of the incident by a staff person unless the home notifies the Department in writing that an extension is necessary and the reason for the extension.
required_items.cite: RCG p.28; §6400.18(i). 18j(1)-(6) lists the required final-report contents. PART B.

required_items.text: The home shall review and analyze incidents and conduct and document a trend analysis at least every 3 months.
required_items.cite: RCG p.30; §6400.20(b). PART B. Related: 20a(1)-(3) cause analysis, corrective action and risk strategy for each confirmed incident; 20c(1)-(3) preventive measures; 20d educate staff and the individual; 20e monitor incidents and take actions to mitigate and manage risks.

required_items.text: (a) An application for a Pennsylvania criminal history record check shall be submitted to the State Police for prospective employees of the home who will have direct contact with individuals, including part-time and temporary staff persons who will have direct contact with individuals, within 5 working days after the person's date of hire. (b) If a prospective employee who will have direct contact with individuals resides outside this Commonwealth, an application for a Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) criminal history record check shall be submitted to the FBI in addition to the Pennsylvania criminal history record check within 5 working days after the person's date of hire. (c) The Pennsylvania and FBI criminal history record checks shall have been completed no more than 1 year prior to the person's date of hire.
required_items.cite: RCG pp.30-31; §6400.21(a)-(c). PART B (hiring/personnel policy content). The RCG says OAPSA standards supersede these timeframes. Providers must request checks on or before the first day of work and make a documented case-by-case hiring decision when a record exists.

required_items.text: The home shall inform and explain individual rights and the process to report a rights violation to the individual, and persons designated by the individual, upon admission to the home and annually thereafter.
required_items.cite: RCG p.52; §6400.34(a). PART B (individual rights content). 34b requires keeping the signed acknowledgment.

required_items.text: Program specialists and direct service workers shall be trained before working with individuals in: General fire safety, Evacuation procedures, Responsibilities during fire drills, The designated meeting place outside the building or within the fire safe area in the event of an actual fire, Smoking safety procedures if individuals or staff persons smoke at the home, The use of fire extinguishers, smoke detectors and fire alarms; and Notification of the local fire department as soon as possible after a fire is discovered.
required_items.cite: RCG p.56; §6400.46(a). PART B (training plan content). 46b-46d cover annual fire safety training, first aid, and first aid/Heimlich/CPR.

required_items.text: The orientation must encompass the following areas: 1. The application of: person-centered practices, community integration, individual choice, and supporting individuals to develop and maintain relationships. 2. The prevention, detection and reporting of abuse, suspected abuse and alleged abuse in accordance with the Older Adults Protective Services Act (35 P.S.§§ 10225.101-10225-5102), the Child Protective Service Law (23 Pa.C.S §§ 6301-6386), the Adult Protective Services Act (35 P.S. §§ 10210.101-10210.704) and applicable protective services regulations. 3. Individual rights. 4. Recognizing and reporting incidents. 5. Job-related knowledge and skills.
required_items.cite: RCG p.59; §6400.51(b). PART B (orientation plan). 51a lists who must complete orientation within 30 days of hire and before working alone.

required_items.text: The annual training hours specified in subsections (a) and (b) must encompass the following areas: 1. The application of person-centered practices, community integration, individual choice and supporting individuals to develop and maintain relationships. 2. The prevention, detection and reporting of abuse, suspected abuse and alleged abuse in accordance with the Older Adults Protective Services Act (35 P.S.§§ 10225.101-10225-5102), the Child Protective Service Law (23 Pa.C.S §§ 6301-6386), the Adult Protective Services Act (35 P.S. §§ 10210.101-10210.704) and applicable adult protective services regulations. 3. Individual rights. 4. Recognizing and reporting incidents. 5. The safe and appropriate use of behavior supports if the person works directly with an individual. 6. Implementation of the individual plan if the person works directly with an individual.
required_items.cite: RCG p.61; §6400.52 (the RCG labels this paragraph '6400.52(b)'). PART B (annual training plan). 52a requires 24 hours and 52b requires 12 hours by staff type. The RCG says the provider must establish the training-year dates in writing.

required_items.text: If an individual refuses routine medical or dental examination or treatment, the refusal and continued attempts to train the individual about the need for health care shall be documented in the individual's record.
required_items.cite: RCG p.92; §6400.143(a). PART B. The RCG says licensing staff review 'the provider's procedures for managing individuals' refusals'.

required_items.text: Prescription medications that are discontinued or expired shall be destroyed in a safe manner according to applicable Federal and State statutes and regulations.
required_items.cite: RCG p.100; §6400.163(h). PART B. The RCG says licensing staff review the provider's procedures for disposing of discontinued or expired medications. Medication administration (162, 163, 165-169) and the medication record (166a) are also reviewed in practice, and ODP requires medication administration training under 169.

sections: Home Serving Nine or More Individuals

official.notes: No single policy checklist was machine-readable, so this list is built from the regulation text in the RCG. The only dedicated checklist I found is ODP's 'NEW 6400 Policy Review List' (.docx), whose contents I could not read. It should override this list wherever the two differ. Part A is items the regulation itself says must be written: 22a/22b, 23, 33b, 103, 110h, 114a, 145, 192, and (homes serving 9+) 236 and 243. Part B is items marked 'PART B' in the cite field. In Part B the regulation does not say 'written policy', but the RCG says licensing staff verify them through 'applicable policies' and training records. They cover incident management, abuse and reporting, criminal-history hiring checks, rights notification, and the orientation and annual training topics. Organize the manual by the RCG section order above, using the regulation numbers as headings. Individual-level items are not provider policies and are not listed. They are the dental hygiene plan (142f-h), the behavior support component of the individual plan (195), the individual plan (185), and the individual emergency information (211). The Chapter 20 application and fees, the certificate of occupancy (14a), and the self-assessment (15) are paperwork, not policy content. Also not listed: the regulations' physical-site and fire-safety standards, which licensing staff check by observation of the home. The RCG also gives CEO and program specialist qualifications (43c, 44c) and staffing ratios (45). For waiver-funded Residential Habilitation, ODP provider enrollment adds requirements beyond Chapter 6400. These include Chapter 6100, the ODP Provider Applicant Orientation, the Waiver Provider Agreement and the New Provider Self-Assessment, and a 5-year manager experience rule for executive staff hired for enrollment. Those requirements are outside this list. The ODP licensing contact in the RCG is RA-odplicensing@pa.gov, and customer service is RA-customerservice@pa.gov or 1-888-565-9435.
